wagyu101.title: Everything you need to know about wagyu
wagyu101.lede: What A5 means, how marbling is graded, and how to choose the right cut.
wagyu101.whatBody: Wagyu (和牛) simply means "Japanese cattle". Four native breeds qualify, and over 90% are Kuroge, Japanese Black. Their genetics produce intramuscular fat that melts at a lower temperature than other beef, giving wagyu its buttery texture and sweet aroma.
wagyu101.gradeBody: The Japan Meat Grading Association scores every carcass twice: a yield grade (A, B or C: how much usable meat) and a quality grade (1–5) based on marbling, colour, firmness and fat quality. A5 is the highest on both scales.
wagyu101.ausBody: Australia raises the largest wagyu herd outside Japan. Its marble score (MB) is broadly comparable to BMS. Australian wagyu is usually crossbred or long-fed fullblood, beefier and leaner than A5, and a great everyday luxury.
wagyu101.cutsLede: Tap a cut to see what it's like and shop it.
wagyu101.traceBody: Every Japanese wagyu carcass has a 10-digit individual ID. It's printed on your certificate of authenticity, and you can look it up in the National Livestock Breeding Center's database to see the farm, breed and birth date.

about.title: Bringing real wagyu to Pakistan
about.body: Wagyu Meat started with a simple frustration: the "wagyu" on Pakistani menus was rarely the real thing, and there was no honest way to buy it at home. We work directly with halal-certified exporters in Japan and Australia, import with full documentation, and deliver frozen through our own cold chain. Every A5 steak comes with its certificate, so you can check its farm yourself.
